The Rust DLL. Also called the broker.

Transport to consumer. Framed protobuf over TCP.

Interface A as a replaceable boundary.

Keeps DCSBridge.state.

Someone extending the bridge with their own files and messages.

on, command, send, off, replace, wrap.
The hook driver or the sim driver, registering topic tables.
The mission-load window. Measured as a total absence of frames, not slow frames.
A record addressed to one connection.
Delivery of a record to every connection.
Saved Games DCS folder, resolved from lfs.writedir.
type.googleapis.com/<package>.<Message>. The topic, and protobuf's own type identity.
google.protobuf.Any. Carries the payload opaquely plus its type URL.
Full name of the same.
The framed outer message: seq, epoch, mission_time and an Any payload.
Buffered emission addressed to one connection. How a handler answers a command.
Versions the Interface C payload grammar. Deliberately not STATE_VERSION.
The bridge's LIFECYCLE record carrying this theatre's DCS-local to lat/lon conversion.
Informal name for the same.
The interval between onSimulationFrame callbacks. Measured as a distribution per phase.
A load or teardown blackout, credited to the phase in force when it began. Not a transition record.
A record describing a change rather than a state: a destruction, a capture, a slot change. Must be idempotent at the consumer.
A change of lifecycle phase. Sections 5.2 and 9.
A record reporting a world change, which must be idempotent at the consumer. Section 6.8.
A per-frame cap held non-binding by invariant, kept so Section 6.4's rule has no exception.
Theatre, name and filename, all readable from the hook driver at onMissionLoadBegin.
DCS.getMissionFilename(). The real path, and the value to scope a file on.
Short for the same.
DCS.getMissionName(). For showing a human, never for identity.
What getMissionName returns for a mission flown from the Mission Editor, whatever the .miz is called.
Hook callback opening the load blackout. Mission identity already reads here.
Hook callback closing the blackout. The hook driver allocates the epoch and emits EpochOpened here.
Hook callback where the hook driver emits EpochClosed. The theatre reads nil by this point.
A file planted under a plausible auto-load name to test whether anything runs it. None did.
An open question with a named measurement.
An external document. Referenced, never defined here.
The record and command set shipped in a driver .builtin.lua file.
What ships in HookDriver.builtin.lua.
Lua debug.sethook instruction hook. Not the hook driver.
A nested message opened with shim.message and closed with shim.end_message.
The transverse Mercator parameter string CoordinateCalibration carries.
A point a consumer checks the published projection against.
Magnetic declination, optional per verification point, read from magvar in the GUI state.
The CLI binary.
An external document, the sim driver built-ins. Referenced, never defined here.
An external document, the hook driver built-ins. Referenced, never defined here.
env.mission.date, the simulated date. Carried on CoordinateCalibration. Not the os.time() value on EpochOpened.
The projection keys on terrain; the declination keys on terrain and mission date.
Rejected reason for a command the inbound ring had no room for. Capped by busy_max_per_sec.
The broker-answered request that narrows what a connection is sent. Not Section 6.7.
The per-connection topic set applied at fan-out beside the capability filter.
TopicFilterMode member. The default: every fan-out record the capability set permits.
TopicFilterMode member. The named topics plus every LIFECYCLE topic.
Topic ids one SetTopicFilter may name.
A topic the class table holds. What a topic filter may admit.
TopicFilterResult field. Covers unregistered and capability-uncovered alike, deliberately.
The BUSY rate cap, separate from rejected_max_per_sec.
Why a declination is absent: policy, Route B, or a failed call.
Proleptic Gregorian year, month and day from env.mission.date. No timezone.
The LIFECYCLE set delivered to each newly authenticated connection, in emit order, before any live record. How a reconnecting consumer gets the calibration.
The broker-answered request listing the topics a connection can see. Not GetSchema, which serves the build.
A point-to-point reply the broker produces. Classless, treated as DURABLE by the drop rule.
The per-connection single-producer queue by which the reader thread hands a broker answer to the writer thread.
